title: Freaks

evidence.note: The Catalog of Copyright Entries, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, Jan-Dec 1959, lists a renewal for this film. The entry shows FREAKS, registered 23FEB32 as L2870, claimant Loew's, Inc., renewed 2MAR59 as R252434. The registration date, claimant and title match this 1932 film. A renewal filed in the 28th year of the original term keeps US copyright for the full 95-year term.

editorial:
Freaks is a 1932 film directed by Tod Browning. Its plot, per the Internet Archive's description, follows the trapeze artist Cleopatra, who marries the circus performer Hans once she learns of his inheritance. She plans to steal his fortune and run off with her lover.

The rights trap is that this film was renewed. The 1959 Catalog of Copyright Entries lists a renewal of the 23 February 1932 registration (L2870), filed 2 March 1959 as R252434 by Loew's, Inc. That keeps the film under US copyright. I did not research the music separately. A copy on the Internet Archive is not a rights clearance. Anyone reusing the film should license it from the current rights holder. I did not confirm who that is.
faq: Is Freaks (1932) public domain in the US?
No. The 1959 Catalog of Copyright Entries records a renewal of the film's 1932 registration, filed by Loew's, Inc. as R252434. The film is still under US copyright.
Can I reuse the Internet Archive copy of Freaks?
No, not on the strength of its being online. Uploaded copies are not a rights clearance, and the film's copyright was renewed. Get a licence from the current rights holder before reusing it.
